de25_location.topic: Location data: bidstream, brokers sold to government, carriers, Hemisphere/DAS, court limits

claims.text: FTC proposed order 9 Jan 2024 against X-Mode/Outlogic: sold precise location tied to mobile advertising IDs, not anonymised; clients included private government contractors; no sensitive-location filtering until May 2023; vote 3-0

FTC technology blog 3 Dec 2024: ad auctions broadcast consumer data, sometimes including location, to dozens of bidders in milliseconds; Mobilewalla allegedly kept data from auctions it lost; 'location data is sensitive data, full stop'

FTC final order vs Gravy Analytics and Venntel, 14 Jan 2025, 5-0: bans sale/use of sensitive location data except in limited national security or law enforcement circumstances; complaint alleged collection without consent for commercial and government uses

CBP paid just under $476,000 for Venntel software on 5 Aug 2020; Venntel sells app-derived phone movements searchable by area or device ID; WSJ Feb 2020 reported agencies used it for border crossings and arrests; IRS-CI used Venntel for a year and located no targets (Wyden's office)

DHS OIG-23-61 (Sept 2023): CBP, ICE and Secret Service did not follow DHS privacy policy or obtain Privacy Impact Assessments required by the E-Government Act before buying commercial telemetry data; shared passwords, no supervisory review; a CBP employee used the data to track coworkers (reported 20 Aug 2020); recommended ICE stop using it until PIAs approved

404 Media 8 Jan 2026: ICE's Penlink Webloc can watch a neighbourhood for phones and follow devices over time, from data on hundreds of millions of phones; an internal ICE legal analysis said it can be queried without a warrant

70 members of Congress wrote to DHS IG Cuffari on 3 Mar 2026 asking for a probe of ICE location purchases incl. the no-bid Penlink contract with a Webloc licence; ICE cancelled a hearing appearance in Feb 2026

EFF/AP 1 Sep 2022: Fog Data Science sold police app-derived location histories, claiming billions of points on 250m+ devices, for under $10,000 a year; at least 18 agency clients; searches often without warrants

FBI Director Patel told the Senate on 18 Mar 2026 'We do purchase commercially available information that is consistent with the Constitution and the laws'; Wray had said in 2023 the FBI previously bought location data but was not currently doing so

FCC fined carriers in Apr 2024 for selling customer location to aggregators without consent: AT&T ~$57m, Verizon ~$46.9m, T-Mobile $80m, Sprint ~$12m (~$200m total); the Supreme Court upheld the AT&T and Verizon fines 8-1 on 4 Jun 2026 (Roberts; Thomas dissenting), rejecting the jury-trial challenge; Fifth Circuit had sided with AT&T, Second Circuit with FCC

Wyden letter 20 Nov 2023: Hemisphere (2009-13 name) / Data Analytical Services pays AT&T to search domestic call records back to 1987, ~4bn records added daily, 'trillions' of records; searches often by subpoena; ONDCP funding paused 2013, resumed 2017, paused 2021, $270k in 2022

Chatrie v. United States, 29 Jun 2026: Kagan for five, Gorsuch concurring in judgment, Alito, Thomas, Barrett dissenting; accessing Google Location History via geofence is a search; warrant's probable cause and particularity remanded; 150 m radius, one hour around a bank robbery; Google moved Location History on-device in 2023

Judge Carlton Reeves (S.D. Miss.), Aug 2026: tower-dump warrants are general warrants and per se unconstitutional; upheld magistrate's denials of requests for towers near nine crime scenes; 'The government cannot have access to an entire haystack because it may contain a needle'

NYT, early September 2013: DEA's Hemisphere programme, launched 2007, embedded AT&T staff with drug agents, records back to 1987; a slide told officials to 'never refer to Hemisphere in any official document'

de25_spyware.topic: Spyware, phone extraction and cell-site simulators

claims.text: FORCEDENTRY (NSO, 2021) reached iPhones through iMessage with only a number or Apple ID; a file named .gif was parsed as a PDF with JBIG2 data; an integer overflow let attackers build a small computer from 70,000+ JBIG2 commands; patched 13 Sep 2021 (iOS 14.8, CVE-2021-30860); 'one of the most technically sophisticated exploits we've ever seen'

Amnesty Security Lab found a Cellebrite UFED-linked zero-day chain (USB driver flaws, CVE-2024-53104 etc.) used to unlock a Serbian student activist's Samsung phone in police custody on 25 Dec 2024, followed by an attempt to install spyware; Cellebrite suspended 'certain Serbian customers' on 25 Feb 2025
NSO published a transparency report on 8 Jan 2026 seeking US government business; its 2025 bid to leave the Entity List was reported denied; no US government customer reported

DHS OIG-23-17 (2023): Secret Service and ICE did not always adhere to statute and policy on cell-site simulators; recommendations on distinguishing policy exigency from statutory emergencies and on documenting data deletion

ICE bought cell-site simulator vehicles from TOSV: $818,000 (Sep 2024) and $825,000 modification (8 May 2025); ICE used simulators at least 466 times 2017-19 (ACLU) and 1,885+ times 2013-17 (BuzzFeed)

DOJ policy 3 Sep 2015: warrant on probable cause required for cell-site simulators, with exigent/exceptional exceptions; data deleted once the device is located and at least daily; no content collection

DHS forecast (May 2026): five-year ICE/HSI IDIQ with Cellebrite, $100m ceiling, phones and drones; HSI calls its extraction tool 'the most widely utilized and deployed computer forensic tool'; Cellebrite says use requires valid legal authorization

HSI signed a $3m Magnet Forensics licence contract (Sep 2025), likely GrayKey, plus smaller GrayKey renewals; a $5m GrayKey contract in 2024 reported by Forbes; ICE declined to say if used on arrested migrants' phones
CBP searched a record 55,318 electronic devices in FY2025, up about 17% on the prior year; basic searches 50,922; searches of US citizens' devices 13,590

Italy: Rome and Naples prosecutors confirmed in March 2026 that Fanpage journalist Francesco Cancellato's phone was hacked (Graphite per Citizen Lab); could not confirm for Ciro Pellegrino; COPASIR (June 2025) found targeting of Mediterranea activists lawful; Paragon cancelled contracts with AISE/AISI and had not answered prosecutors as of April 2026; Meloni government denies hacking journalists

de25_cars_home.topic: Cars, wearables, smart home: collection, state access and enforcement

claims.text: FTC final order vs GM/OnStar (Jan 2026, 2-0): 20-year order; five-year ban on sharing geolocation and driver-behaviour data with consumer reporting agencies; affirmative express consent; access, deletion, ability to disable precise geolocation; first-responder exception; Khan said data was sometimes collected every 3 seconds

NYT (Kashmir Hill, 11 Mar 2024): GM driving data (hard braking, acceleration, miles) reached LexisNexis and insurers; reports ran to hundreds of pages; a salesman said he always clicked yes on enrolment; GM ended broker sharing and Smart Driver
Texas AG sued GM (Aug 2024): trip data from most 2015-and-newer GM vehicles sold to firms, at least two producing 'Driving Scores' for insurers; over 1.5m Texans

Wyden-Markey letter 30 Apr 2024: GM, Honda, Ford, Tesla, Stellantis require a warrant for location (absent emergency/consent); Hyundai warrant or court order; Toyota, Nissan, Subaru, BMW, Mazda, Mercedes-Benz, Kia disclose on subpoena; VW subpoena up to 6 days; Hyundai keeps location up to 15 years, Toyota 10, Honda 7; only Tesla notifies customers; Tesla receives location only for 'a critical safety event'

Tesla law-enforcement guidelines: requests need legal basis or consent; emergency disclosure on good-faith belief of 'danger of death or serious physical injury'; preservation 90 days plus one 90-day extension; reasonable efforts to notify customers unless barred by order

Reuters 7 Apr 2023: nine former Tesla employees said staff shared customer car-camera recordings in internal chats 2019-2022, incl. intimate scenes and a crash with a child; seven said the tool showed where recordings were made; Tesla notice says recordings 'remain anonymous and are not linked to you or your vehicle'; Tesla did not respond

Oakland police obtained court orders to tow Teslas in at least three 2024 incidents to retrieve Sentry Mode footage stored on in-car USB; footage from a 13 July shooting helped charge two suspects with murder

After the 1 Jan 2025 Las Vegas Cybertruck explosion, Sheriff McMahill said Musk sent Tesla charging-station footage directly to investigators and explained how the vehicle locked; Musk posted that vehicle telemetry was positive; no legal process reported
Blumenthal letters 5 Feb 2025 asked Tesla and other Musk firms whether they received nonpublic data from DOGE or supplied servers/AI models; the letters are questions, not evidence of transfer

Berla iVe extracts texts, call logs, contacts, GPS and door/ignition events from 20,752 vehicle types (Mar 2022); CBP paid $450k+ for five kits (Intercept 2021); DHS said in 2023 it 'no longer partners' with Berla; courts in at least six states allowed warrantless vehicle downloads
HSI sole-source notice 28 Aug 2026 to renew Berla iVe (after ~$130k 2025 order); Sep 2025 award of $311,250 for 325 Ensurity covert GPS trackers
Connie Dabate was killed 23 Dec 2015; her Fitbit showed movement about an hour after the time her husband said she was shot; he was sentenced to 65 years on 18 Aug 2022
Jury found Meta violated CIPA by collecting Flo users' menstrual data (5 Aug 2025); Google and Flo settled; Meta 'vigorously disagree[s]'

Apple: Health app data is end-to-end encrypted with recent OS, 2FA and passcode, 'not readable by anyone — even Apple'; Apple 'does not sell' consumer health data; disclosure 'when required by applicable law'

Kennedy, 24 Jun 2025: wearables are 'a way people can take control of their own health'; promised a large HHS campaign; 'within the next four years' is reporters' paraphrase; consumer wearable data is outside HIPAA and governed by terms of service

Washington My Health My Data Act: passed Apr 2023, effective Mar 2024, covers health status, biometric and precise location data, private right of action; first suit Maxwell v. Amazon (10 Feb 2025) over an ad SDK
FTC/NJ vs Vizio, 6 Feb 2017: $2.2m; 11m TVs captured second-by-second viewing data since Feb 2014, added demographics and sold to third parties without consent

Texas AG sued Sony, Samsung, LG, Hisense and TCL (Dec 2025) alleging ACR screenshots 'as often as every half second'; Samsung settled by Mar 2026, agreeing not to collect ACR data from Texans without explicit informed consent
Amazon ended 'Do Not Send Voice Recordings' on 28 Mar 2025 for Echo Dot 4th gen, Echo Show 10 and 15, sending all recordings to the cloud for Alexa+

Bates (Bentonville, Ark.): Amazon refused Echo data without a valid legal demand, released it after Bates consented; a smart water meter showed night-time use; charges dropped by nolle prosequi in Nov 2017

FTC, May-June 2023: Alexa $25m COPPA penalty (children's recordings kept); Ring $5.8m refunds — an employee viewed thousands of female users' videos incl. bathrooms and bedrooms; 55,000+ accounts compromised Jan 2019-Mar 2020
Amazon told Markey (public 13 Jul 2022) Ring gave footage to police without consent 11 times in 2022 on 'imminent danger' findings; 2,161 agencies were on Neighbors

Ring cancelled its planned Flock integration (Feb 2026); says it has no partnership with ICE and federal agencies cannot submit Community Requests; local police requests run through Axon Evidence and owners may decline

Guthrie case (Feb 2026): FBI Director Patel said Nest video was 'recovered from residual data located in backend systems'; the sheriff said she had no subscription that would save video; Google gave no details

claims.text: DHS told NPR (May 2026) 'ICE has no relationship with Paragon Solutions, Inc. or with the company that acquired them' and had not entered another contract; a procurement notice shows the contract closed out 20 Jan 2026; DHS would 'not … confirm or deny' capabilities; Lyons (1 Apr 2026) said he approved HSI's procurement and operational use

ICE agreed in fall 2025 to pay Penlink $2.3m covering Tangles (AI open-source intelligence incl. face detection) and Webloc (search an area and time for phone movements, trace a phone); ICE bought licences, not the company; Spire Capital controlling investor since 2022; Penlink acquired Cobwebs in 2023; Penlink: tools 'exclusively use publicly or commercially available data'

Guardian (Just Futures Law FOIA, 2014-2022 ICE/HSI documents): agents could import Cellebrite phone extractions into Palantir tools and search SEVIS (4.9m records) and APIS; NCIC listed as import source; CLEAR not natively connected; Palantir calls itself a 'data processor'

Letter of 14 Apr 2026 (33 signatories incl. Goldman, Velázquez, Wyden) to DHS and ICE asks which government and commercial datasets are in Palantir-developed systems; names ELITE, Clearview, PenLink, L3Harris Stingray and Paragon; deadline 24 Apr 2026

ICE notice of intent 10 Aug 2026: ~$6.7m sole-source LexisNexis bridge; work statement requires APIs to ICE applications 'such as but not limited to' the Palantir platform, PenLink and ICE Data Analytics; Accurint Virtual Crime Center includes device-geolocation analysis
